introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2024. Additional Mathematics 2 (code 0575), Paper 2. Duration: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions, questions 1 to 8). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions, questions 9 to 11; if this section is chosen, Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (answer any two questions, questions 12 to 14; if this section is chosen, Section B may not be chosen). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown: 6. (i) Solve for $\theta$, in the range $0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ$, the equation $\cos2\theta=1$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since $0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ$, the angle $2\theta$ lies in $0^\circ\le2\theta\le720^\circ$.

$\cos2\theta=1$ when $2\theta=0^\circ,\;360^\circ,\;720^\circ$.

Divide by $2$: $\theta=0^\circ,\;180^\circ,\;360^\circ$.

Check: $\cos0^\circ=1$, $\cos360^\circ=1$, $\cos720^\circ=1$.

**Answer: $\theta=0^\circ,\,180^\circ,\,360^\circ$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) The function $f(x)$ is defined by $f(x)=\sin x+\cos x$, where $0\le x\le2\pi$.

a) Copy and complete the table below. *[3 marks]*

| $x$ | $0$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ | $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ | $\pi$ | $\dfrac{5\pi}{4}$ | $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ | $\dfrac{7\pi}{4}$ | $2\pi$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f(x)$ | $1$ |  | $1$ | $0$ |  | $-1.4$ |  | $0$ |  |
(ii)(b) Taking $1$ cm to represent $\dfrac\pi4$ radians on the $x$-axis and $2$ cm to represent $1$ unit on the $y$-axis, draw the graph of $y=f(x)$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Scales.** On the $x$-axis, $1$ cm $=\dfrac\pi4$, so the nine table values of $x$ are at $0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8$ cm. On the $y$-axis, $2$ cm $=1$ unit, so $y=1$ is $2$ cm up and $y=1.4$ is $2.8$ cm up.

**Points to plot** (distance along the $x$-axis, height):

| $x$ | $0$ | $\frac\pi4$ | $\frac\pi2$ | $\frac{3\pi}4$ | $\pi$ | $\frac{5\pi}4$ | $\frac{3\pi}2$ | $\frac{7\pi}4$ | $2\pi$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| position (cm) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
| $f(x)$ | 1 | 1.4 | 1 | 0 | -1 | -1.4 | -1 | 0 | 1 |
| height (cm) | 2 | 2.8 | 2 | 0 | -2 | -2.8 | -2 | 0 | 2 |

Join the points with a **smooth curve**: it is one full wave of a sine-shaped curve, starting at $(0,1)$, rising to a maximum of about $1.4$ at $x=\frac\pi4$, crossing the $x$-axis at $x=\frac{3\pi}4$, reaching a minimum of about $-1.4$ at $x=\frac{5\pi}4$, crossing the axis again at $x=\frac{7\pi}4$, and ending at $(2\pi,1)$. (Since $\sin x+\cos x=\sqrt2\sin\!\big(x+\frac\pi4\big)$, the amplitude is $\sqrt2$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) Write down the minimum value of $f(x)$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
From the graph (or from $f(x)=\sqrt2\sin\!\big(x+\frac\pi4\big)$) the lowest point is at $x=\dfrac{5\pi}{4}$.

**Answer: the minimum value of $f(x)$ is $-\sqrt2\approx-1.4$** (at $x=\frac{5\pi}4$).
